clue.text: Cook burned a lot – no square meals for sir here?

definitions.text: no square meals for sir here

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or fiddle, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A kitchen disaster: the cook has charred so much that there are no proper meals for the gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: not square means round, meals suggests a table, and Arthur's knights, each a Sir, sat at the Round Table.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's knights, all titled Sir, gathered at a circular board so none sat at its head.

clue.text: Hitch – or thriller he directed?

blocks.note: first meaning: to tie up or fasten, as with a cord
second meaning: a 1948 Hitchcock film, 'he' pointing back to Hitch as the director's nickname

explanation.walkthrough: Hitch is also Alfred Hitchcock's nickname, so the 'he' of the second half cleverly refers back to the first word read another way.
explanation.definitionFit: To rope something is to tie or hitch it, and Rope is Hitchcock's single-set murder thriller.

clue.text: NUT leader changed and not changed

indicators.note: if something is changed its order is altered, so the preceding letters get rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A teachers' union (the NUT) gets a new leader yet nothing really changes.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the paradox of changed and not changed; the first is the signal, the second the definition. The NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaltered describes something left exactly as it was, untouched by any modification.

clue.text: Fine arts Donne misused for hellish rhyme?

indicators.note: words that are misused are put wrongly, so these letters are set in a different order

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that the poetry of John Donne is being abused in the cause of the fine arts.
explanation.walkthrough: Donne looks like part of the definition, being a poet, but his name is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inferno is the first part of Dante's Divine Comedy, a poem in terza rima describing a journey through Hell.

clue.text: Million American recluse invests for old social worker

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or wrap, so the recluse word goes around the million abbreviation

explanation.surface: A rich American hermit puts money into a charitable cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Million comes first in the clue but sits inside the recluse word; the American letter goes at the very front.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was formerly a hospital social worker, and earlier someone who distributed alms to the poor.

clue.text: Really sloshed – on not as many?

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A drinker so far gone they can barely keep count of the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: On = LEG is a cricket convention: the on side and leg side are the same half of the field. Legless is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone legless is so intoxicated they cannot stand, slang for extremely drunk.

clue.text: State secrets in British science establishment

explanation.surface: Official state secrets held at a British research facility.
explanation.walkthrough: State secrets reads as a noun phrase about government; here state is a verb meaning tell.
explanation.definitionFit: To blab is to reveal confidences carelessly, telling secrets that should be kept.

clue.text: Old Italian bread surrounding duck in river

indicators.note: surrounding means wrapping around, so the currency word encloses the duck

blocks.note: bread is slang for money; the lira was Italy's currency before the euro
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so zero

explanation.surface: A stale Italian loaf wrapped around a duck, perhaps for a riverside meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is the money, not the food.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is France's longest river, flowing past many chateaux to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Slug covering new open space in country

indicators.note: covering means lying over and around, so the slug word wraps the rest

blocks.note: to slug someone is to hit them hard

explanation.surface: A slug crawling across a freshly opened stretch of ground somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Slug looks like the garden creature but it is a verb for punching.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangladesh is a South Asian nation on the Bay of Bengal.

clue.text: Obvious scheme to snare Independent

indicators.note: to snare is to trap, so the scheme word closes around the other letter

explanation.surface: An obvious plot to trap an independent politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain is clear and easily seen, so evident.

clue.text: Russian fighter helping diaspora

blocks.note: a MiG is a Soviet-designed fighter jet

explanation.surface: A Russian soldier assisting a scattered people.
explanation.walkthrough: Helping looks like a verb but is a noun, a serving.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is the scattering of a people from their homeland, a large-scale movement of population.

clue.text: See 12
Dungeon, knife etc: Arthur endlessly tortured in story

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the king's name is dropped
tortured means twisted out of shape, so all these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the name minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A grim scene: King Arthur being tormented in a dungeon with a knife and other instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur himself is the subject of the answer, which makes the clue nearly self-describing.
explanation.definitionFit: T. H. White's novel sequence retelling the Arthurian legend bears this title, from Arthur's supposed epitaph.

clue.text: Live and prosper – nothing to lose

indicators.note: having something to lose means it gets taken away from the phrase before

blocks.note: to do well is to thrive

explanation.surface: A twist on the Vulcan greeting from Star Trek, live long and prosper, with a carefree attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Live and prosper looks like one phrase; live alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside or make one's home there.

clue.text: Squared up? Romeo bruised me badly!

indicators.note: doing something badly means doing it wrongly, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Juliet complains that Romeo hurt her and then settled the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Squared up is a colloquial way of settling a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reimbursed is to be paid back money owed, so accounts are squared.

clue.text: Organ that is grasped in both hands, further back?

indicators.note: something grasped in the hands is held between them, so it sits inside

explanation.surface: An organ held carefully in a surgeon's two hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a time further back, before the present.

clue.text: Puzzled out?

blocks.note: first meaning: baffled, at a loss
second meaning: a cricket dismissal where the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while the batter is out of the crease

explanation.walkthrough: Puzzled out reads as solved, but the two words are separate meanings; the second is a cricketing way to be dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumped means baffled, and in cricket a batter is stumped when the keeper removes the bails.

clue.text: See 21
Cricketers in field annoy son holding party

indicators.note: holding means having inside, so the annoy word encloses the party word

explanation.surface: Someone irritates their son by hosting a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-off is a cricket fielding position near the bowler on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-offs are fielders stationed in that position, so cricketers out in the field.

clue.text: Maybe Sevillian cross is above hotel

indicators.note: in a down entry being above means coming before, so these parts follow in order

blocks.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone from Seville is angry about where they are staying.
explanation.definitionFit: Seville is a city in Spain, so a Sevillian is one example of a Spanish person.

clue.text: Star formula not for backward graduate

indicators.note: not means without, so the word after is taken out
going backward means reading right to left

explanation.surface: A slow graduate fails to find the star formula.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for is removed from formula, then the whole string runs right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a former student of a school or university, typically one who has graduated.

clue.text: First man allowed to start with Bible books firm

indicators.note: to start means only the opening letter is wanted

explanation.surface: Adam was permitted to begin reading the scriptures with conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unyielding and resolute, as firm in an opinion as hard stone.

clue.text: King united there with knight: fiery monster seizing power

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the power letter is taken inside the rest

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A king joins up with a knight at the scene of a fire-breathing beast that is grabbing power.
explanation.walkthrough: Power goes inside the whole string joined so far, just after its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Uther Pendragon is the legendary British king who fathered King Arthur.

clue.text: Marx collaborator in male set

explanation.surface: A collaborator of Marx found among a group of men.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: Hegel died before Marx's career began, but Marx built directly on Hegel's dialectic. Engels was the actual collaborator.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegel's dialectical philosophy was the foundation Marx reworked, so a posthumous partner in his thought.

clue.text: Hobbyist in a chess defeat – game over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the game letters run the other way

explanation.surface: A casual player is checkmated, and the game ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur pursues an activity for pleasure rather than payment, as a hobbyist does.

clue.text: Ear's twitching after ring

definitions.note: the possessive stands for an adjective meaning of the ear

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the twitching word follows the ring

blocks.note: a ring is round like the letter

explanation.surface: Someone's ear starts twitching after a phone rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is a medical term meaning relating to the ear.

clue.text: Men in area chasing token girl in Rome

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so these parts come after the token word

explanation.surface: Men in a district pursue a girl only as a token gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: In looks like a linking preposition but is taken literally as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Signorina is the Italian word for an unmarried young woman, so a Roman girl.

clue.text: Bar showing other shows

indicators.note: shows means displays, so the letters are visible within the neighbouring words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A pub or theatre bar screening other programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a bar of cast metal, typically gold.

clue.text: Exterminator sparing a thousand in valley

indicators.note: sparing means doing without, so the thousand letter is dropped

blocks.note: Doctor Who's robotic villains whose catchphrase is Exterminate

explanation.surface: A killer shows mercy to a thousand people in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Daleks are the alien villains of the British TV series Doctor Who, famous for shrieking Exterminate.
explanation.definitionFit: A dale is a valley, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Posed on the go in shot like Kate Moss?

indicators.note: posed means arranged in a position, so the letters are put in a new order
in means placed inside, so the rearranged letters go within the picture word

explanation.surface: A busy model caught posing in a quick snap.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate Moss is a celebrated British supermodel, so the question mark marks her as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A photogenic person looks attractive in photographs, as a top fashion model must.
